rationale:
M14 ONTOLOGY (2026-10-04), the `exports` type, and the measurement that FORBIDS the easy ruling. The tempting verdict is RULED: 'C++ has no export construct.' The census says otherwise on two counts. (a) The construct is spelled twice — `__declspec(dllexport)` (MSVC) and `__attribute__((visibility("default")))` (GCC/Clang ELF) — and the pinned grammar reads BOTH as nodes: `ms_declspec_modifier` carries the attribute names as named children, and `attribute_specifier` carries an `argument_list` whose `call_expression` names `visibility`. Over the corpus: 1 inline `visibility("default")` site (in a file named `test/static-export-test/library.cc`, whose purpose is to export a symbol that way) and 11 `#define X __declspec(dllexport)` definitions. (b) A ruling needs the construct to be ABSENT, and `ontology-coverage-gate.ts` fails a ruling whose probe finds a non-zero count — so ruling this was falsifiable, and falsified.

What IS ruled, with the count: C++20 modules. Measured on the pinned grammar: 0 `export`, `module_declaration`, `import_declaration` and `module_import` nodes across 182 node types, and `export module M;` ERROR-recovers into `declaration[declarator=module, type=export]` — a recovery artifact the analyzer must not read as an export.

What is NOT emitted, and said so rather than left to be re-derived: the macro-mediated arm. 11 corpus sites write the attribute behind a `#define` (`FMT_API`, `GTEST_API_`, `JSON_HEDLEY_PUBLIC`, `EXPORT_ATTR`), which is how real libraries do it, and reading them needs macro expansion — a DECLARED limitation of this lane (M14-HONESTY-CONTRACT §3, 'macro/template expansion boundaries'). The last declaration in this fixture asserts that boundary as an absence, so the limitation is pinned rather than assumed.

Five negative arms, each a shape a looser rule would swallow: the OPPOSITE spellings (`dllimport` imports from another module; `visibility("hidden")` is the opposite of exported), a bare `__attribute__((unused))` with no visibility in it, a plain function that CALLS something named `visibility`, and a macro-mediated export.

`ExportedClass` and `WithExportedMember.exported_method` pin the two endpoint forms: a class name, and an `Owner.member` composite (the convention `overrides` already uses, so an exported member cannot be confused with a same-named file-scope entity). `Alpha.same_name` and `Beta.same_name` pin that the one-edge-per-pair rule is keyed on the PAIR, so two classes exporting the same method name are two edges.

`cpp/exports-macro-mediated` is the mutant that resolves the `#define`, and this fixture FORBIDS the edge it would add: a limitation that is not pinned is an omission somebody re-derives.

expectRelationships.note: the MSVC arm, read from an `ms_declspec_modifier` node rather than from the attribute text.
the GCC/Clang arm, read from an `attribute_specifier` whose `visibility` call takes `"default"` — the ROLE walk, so a `visibility` that is merely CALLED elsewhere cannot satisfy it.
`__declspec` precedes the type on the specifier, so the row's line is the CLASS NAME's line and not the attribute's — the same #921/#925 rule every other relationship in this lane follows.
a class member exports as `Owner.member`, so it is not confused with a file-scope entity of the same name.
TWO classes exporting the same method name are TWO edges: the one-edge-per-pair rule is keyed on the (owner, name) pair, and these pairs differ.

forbidRelationships.note: NEGATIVE ARM: `__declspec(dllimport)` is the OPPOSITE direction — this translation unit imports the symbol from another module. Measured in the corpus: 2 sites, both `dllimport`, 0 `dllexport`.
NEGATIVE ARM: `visibility("hidden")` is the opposite of default visibility.
NEGATIVE ARM: a bare `__attribute__((unused))` carries no visibility, so it exports nothing. A rule that keyed on 'has an attribute_specifier' would take this.

NEGATIVE ARM: the `visibility` in `return visibility(v)` is a CALLED FUNCTION, not an attribute. Reading the role (a `call_expression` as an attribute argument) is what separates it; a text scan for the word would not.

THE LIMITATION ARM, asserted. `BENCHMARK_EXPORT` expands to `__declspec(dllexport)`, so this declaration IS an export in C++ — and the analyzer does not emit it, because reading it needs macro expansion (M14-HONESTY-CONTRACT §3). 11 corpus sites are in this shape. Pinning the absence is what makes it a measured boundary rather than an omission; `cpp/exports-macro-mediated` is the mutant that breaks it on purpose.
a member without the attribute is not exported — the arm that separates 'the class has an exported member' from 'every member is exported'.
and it is not published under a bare name either: there is no file-scope entity called `plain_method` to export.

SPELLING CONTRACT (L-2026-10-21-07): a defect that re-spells this end of the row as the owner-qualified spelling would NOT be caught by the bare-spelling forbid beside it, so the spelling is pinned here too.
